3. His case, in short, was that one Shudir Chandra Roy was recorded tenant in respect of the land of plot No. 1743 with an area 58 decimals. Of said land, the preemptor purchased 28 decimals along with 39 decimals of land of plot No. 1741 by registered Kabala being No. 2916 dated 12-10-65. He also purchased 1.70 acres of land by 2 kabalas dated 18-11-66 and 2-2-73 from the same owner, which were adjacent to the case plot. By purchase he became a co-sharer in the case holding being khatian No. 89(66). 

 4. After purchase, the preemptor got his land mutated in his name and opened a separate khatian in separation case No. 759 of 1977. He became a co-sharer tenant in the case holding. 

 17. The trial Court found that the preemptor was though not entitled to pre-empt as a co-sharer by purchase since he got his purchased land mutated in a separate khatian but was entitled to as an owner holding land contiguous to the land transferred.
